paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Some of the scribes and Pharisees asked Jesus for a sign, even after He had healed a man who was blind and mute (Matthew 12:22, 38). Jesus answered that none would be given except the sign of the prophet Jonah, and then He pointed to Himself: the Son of Man will be "three days and three nights in the heart of the earth" (Matthew 12:39-40). The biggest sign was never going to be a trick to impress people. It was Jesus Himself, and He is the answer.

Jesus says the men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonah and the Queen of the South came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and then He says, "now One greater than Jonah is here" and "One greater than Solomon is here" (Matthew 12:41-42). They were sitting right in front of Jesus and still asking for more proof, when I would have been the first one dusting off my apron to listen. The picture of the swept-clean house shows that a house made tidy and left empty is not enough (Matthew 12:43-45). Being near Jesus isn't the goal, and welcoming Him is.

Then comes the part that gets me every time. When someone tells Jesus His mother and brothers are outside, He points to His disciples and says, "For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother" (Matthew 12:48-50). So the invitation is wide open to anyone who does the will of His Father. You don't earn a seat by being impressive, baker. You get a place in His family by listening to Jesus and doing what He says, and I've got a whole bakery full of cookies that say there's room for you.
